title: The Radio Station
summary: A radio station has three wings: the Programme Wing, the Engineering Wing and the Administration Wing (it provides all the support). The first two run the broadcasts.

Radio studio: a room with a table and a microphone, a heavy door and a sound lock (an enclosed space before the door) that stops unnecessary outside sounds; walls and ceiling have perforated woollen panels; air-conditioned. A station has at least two studios; the second is the announcer's booth or transmission studio, where the announcer sits at a microphone with a computer, CD players, tape decks and a mixer. Control Room (CR): the main technical area connected with all segments; whatever is spoken in the studio or played from CD or computer reaches the control room, where technical people control the process, and it is sent to the transmitter. Flow: Studio → Control Room → Transmitter (XTR) → Listener. Transmitter: the equipment through which we receive the broadcast on our sets; its strength decides the coverage area; Low Power Transmitters (LPT, e.g. 1 KW, installed near the studio) and High Power Transmitters (HPT, 100, 200, 250 KW or above, located outside the city boundaries); Medium Wave (MW) and Short Wave (SW) transmitters.

Station Director: in charge of the station and head of the programme wing (called manager in some stations). Station Engineer: heads the engineering wing and is responsible for all technical work; engineers and technicians operate and maintain equipment and oversee the control room. Programme personnel (programme executives or producers): plan, produce, prepare and present programmes. Transmission staff (transmission executives): smooth, trouble-free transmission. Radio announcer: presents programmes and makes them interesting, conveying feeling through voice only (Amin Sayani of Binaca Geetmala). Artists: vocalists and instrumentalists, graded by experience.

All India Radio (AIR), officially Akashvani, is a division of Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India), an autonomous corporation under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; headquarters at Akashvani Bhawan, New Delhi; one of the largest radio networks in the world. Vividh Bharati offers news, film music and comedy. AIR has a three-tier system: national (National channel started 18 May 1988 with transmitters at Nagpur, Mogra and Delhi, Hindi, English and Urdu, reaching about 76% of the population), regional (stations in states including the North-eastern service at Shillong) and local radio (area-specific, intimate, the mouthpiece of the local community). FM (Frequency Modulation) channels of AIR: FM Rainbow (12 channels) and FM Gold (4 channels), with popular Indian and Western music for urban youth plus news. Private (commercial) FM radio stations such as Radio Mirchi, Radio Mango, Big FM and Times FM have a licence to broadcast and cater to the young with music and fun. Community radio serves a limited, homogenous community with local programmes, mostly developmental, in the local language or dialect; a community radio licence is required; Anna FM, launched on 1 February 2004 at Anna University, Chennai, is India's first campus community radio.

vsa: Discuss the role of the Station Engineer and Radio Announcer in a radio station.
The Station Engineer heads the engineering wing and is responsible for all technical work; the Radio Announcer presents the programmes and makes them interesting through voice.
List any two functionaries of a radio station with their function.
Station Director: in charge of the station and programme wing. Programme producer: plans, produces and presents programmes.

sa: Write a short note on community radio or private radio station.

Community radio serves a limited, homogenous community with developmental programmes in the local language and needs a licence (Anna FM); private radio stations such as Radio Mirchi are licensed commercial stations giving music and fun to the youth.
Describe community radio and its operations. Give an example.

Community radio caters to the interests of a limited area; it needs a licence, produces local-language programmes stressing development though entertainment is allowed; example: Anna FM, India's first campus community radio.
Explain the three-tier system of All India Radio.
National channel (since 18 May 1988; news, plays, music in Hindi, English and Urdu), regional stations (middle tier, including the North-eastern service at Shillong) and local radio (area specific).
Describe the roles of the studio, control room and transmitter.
Studio: sound-proof room where programmes are produced; control room: technical area that sends the programmes to the transmitter; transmitter: sends waves to the listener's radio set.
la: Explain the structure and functioning of a radio station.

Three wings: programme, engineering, administration. Studio (sound lock, woollen panels, announcer's booth) → control room → transmitter → listener. Functionaries: Station Director, Station Engineer, programme staff, transmission staff, announcers and artists.
Describe the role played by different functionaries of a radio station.
Station Director, Station Engineer, technicians, programme executives, transmission executives, announcers and artists each handle planning, technical work, transmission and presentation.
